guides.title: How to Sign a PDF on iPhone (Free, Two Ways)
guides.description: How to sign a PDF on iPhone for free: use Markup in the Files app, or scan and sign with SignSnap. Step by step, no printer and no account.
guides.h1: How to sign a PDF on iPhone
guides.answer: You can sign a PDF on iPhone for free with Markup, which is built into the Files app: open the PDF, tap the Markup button, tap the plus button, choose Add Signature and drag it onto the line. If the document is on paper, or you sign things often, a signing app such as SignSnap scans the page with the camera, keeps your signature ready and adds the date in one tap.

sections.h2: Method 1: Markup in the Files app (built in, free)
sections.intro: Every iPhone can do this without installing anything. It works best when the PDF is already on your phone, for example as an email attachment.
steps: Save the PDF to Files. In Mail, tap the attachment, tap the share button and choose Save to Files.
Open the Files app, find the PDF and tap it to open it.
Tap the Markup button (a pen tip inside a circle).
Tap the plus button, then Add Signature. Sign with your finger and tap Done. iPhone remembers it for next time.
Drag the signature onto the line and drag its corners to make it fit.
Tap Done. Files saves the signature into that PDF. Tap the share button to send it back by Mail or Messages.

sections.h2: Method 2: SignSnap (paper documents and frequent signing)
sections.intro: SignSnap is a free iPhone and iPad app from Graysmith Labs made only for signing. It helps most when you were handed paper, when you sign often, or when you want the date next to your signature.
steps: Open SignSnap and import the PDF from the Files app (save an email attachment to Files first) or Photos, or scan a paper page with the camera. The scanner finds the edges and straightens the page.
Create your signature once: draw it with your finger, or type your name in a script font. You can save your initials the same way; each signing places one mark plus the date.
Place it on the line and pinch to resize it. Tap Date to stamp today's date beside it.
Share the signed PDF to Mail, Messages, AirDrop or Files.
sections.note: No account is needed and documents stay on your iPhone. The first 2 signed documents are free; after that Premium is weekly, monthly or yearly, and new subscribers get a free week.

head: Markup in Files
SignSnap
rows: Scan first in Notes, then open the PDF
Built in scanner, one page at a time
Type it with a text box

sections.after: For a PDF that needs blanks filled in, such as a lease or an application, see how to fill and sign a lease on your phone.

sections.h2: Is a signature made on an iPhone legally valid?
paras: In the United States, the federal ESIGN Act and the state laws based on UETA generally give electronic signatures the same standing as ink for most everyday contracts, including leases, offer letters and permission slips. Some documents are excluded or need more, such as wills, certain court papers and anything that must be notarized.
If you are not sure, ask whoever sent the document whether a signed PDF is acceptable. This guide is general information, not legal advice.

faq: Can I sign a PDF on iPhone without downloading an app?
Yes. Open the PDF in the Files app, tap the Markup button, tap the plus button and choose Add Signature. Drag the signature onto the line and tap Done.
How do I sign a PDF that someone emailed me?

Tap the attachment in Mail, tap the share button and choose Save to Files. Then sign it with Markup in Files, or import it into a signing app such as SignSnap, and share the signed PDF back as a reply.
How do I sign a paper document with my iPhone?
Scan it first. SignSnap has a scanner built in that finds the page edges, so you can scan, sign and send a one page form in one app. For several pages, the Notes app can scan them into one PDF.
Can I add the date next to my signature?
In Markup, tap the plus button, choose Add Text and type the date. In SignSnap, tap Date while placing your signature to stamp today's date.
Does SignSnap upload my documents?
No. SignSnap needs no account and keeps documents on your iPhone. A file leaves the phone only when you share it.

guides.title: How to Fill and Sign a Lease on Your Phone
guides.description: Fill in and sign a rental lease on iPhone: get it as a PDF, type into the blanks, initial and sign each page, and send it back. No printer needed.
guides.h1: How to fill and sign a lease on your phone
guides.answer: To fill and sign a lease on your phone, open the lease PDF in the Files app, type your details into the blanks with Markup, add your initials and signature wherever the lease asks for them, then send the finished PDF back to your landlord. If you were handed paper, scan it into a PDF first.

sections.h2: Step 1: Get the lease as a PDF
paras: If the lease came by email, tap the attachment, tap the share button and choose Save to Files. If your landlord uses a signing service such as DocuSign, follow its link instead; it walks you through every field and you do not need anything else.

If the lease is on paper, scan every page into one PDF with the Notes app (open a note, tap the camera button, choose Scan Documents). SignSnap's scanner also finds the page edges and straightens them, one page at a time, which suits a single signature page. Scan in good light on a dark table so the edges are clear.

sections.h2: Step 2: Read it before you write anything
sections.intro: A phone screen makes it easy to skim. Zoom in and check the parts that cost money later:
list: Rent, the due date, the late fee and how you pay
Security deposit, what it covers and when it comes back
Start date, end date and what happens at the end (renewal or month to month)
Breaking the lease early: notice and fees
Pets, guests, parking and subletting rules
Which utilities you pay and who handles repairs
Every name spelled correctly, including yours

steps: Open the PDF in the Files app and tap the Markup button (a pen tip inside a circle).
If the lease has form fields, tap a field and type. Recent versions of iOS can offer your name, address and phone number from your contact card; check each suggestion before you accept it.
For blanks that are just lines on the page, tap the plus button, choose Add Text, then drag the text box onto the line and type.
Tap Done to save.

paras: Many leases ask for initials on every page or beside certain clauses, and a full signature with the date at the end. Count them before you start so none get missed.
In Markup, save a second signature that is just your initials (plus button, Add Signature), then add it on each page that asks for it, and add your full signature last. Add the date with a text box.

If you scanned a paper lease or only need the final signature, SignSnap does that part in a few taps: draw or type your signature, place it on the line, pinch to resize, and tap Date to stamp today's date. SignSnap places one signature per signing, so for initials on many pages Markup is quicker.

sections.h2: Step 5: Send it back and keep a copy
paras: Scroll through every page once more, then tap the share button and send the PDF back by Mail or Messages. Keep the signed copy in a Files folder you will find again, and ask for a copy signed by the landlord too, since that is the version that binds both of you.

In the United States, electronic signatures are generally valid for leases under the federal ESIGN Act and state laws based on UETA. If your landlord asks for ink, print, sign and scan instead. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq: Can I sign a lease on my iPhone?
Yes. Open the lease PDF in the Files app, tap Markup, then the plus button and Add Signature. Place your signature and initials where the lease asks, tap Done and send the PDF back.
Is a lease signed on a phone legally binding?
In the United States, electronic signatures on leases are generally valid under the ESIGN Act and state laws based on UETA. Ask your landlord if you are unsure, and keep a copy signed by both of you.
How do I type on the lines of a PDF on iPhone?
In Markup, tap the plus button and choose Add Text, then drag the text box onto the line and type. Fillable form fields can be tapped and typed into directly.
What if my landlord gave me a paper lease?

Scan every page into one PDF with the Notes app, then fill and sign the PDF and email it back. If only one page needs your signature, SignSnap can scan and sign that page. Ask whether a signed PDF is acceptable first.
How do I add the date to my signature?
In Markup, add a text box with the date beside your signature. In SignSnap, tap Date while placing your signature.

guides.title: Cloudy Hot Tub Water: Why It Happens and How to Fix It
guides.description: Why is my hot tub water cloudy? Usually low sanitizer, high pH or alkalinity, or a dirty filter. Test, balance, shock and rinse the filter, in that order.
guides.h1: Cloudy hot tub water: why it happens and how to fix it
guides.answer: Cloudy hot tub water almost always comes from low sanitizer, pH or alkalinity that has crept too high, or a clogged filter, and old water full of dissolved solids makes all three worse. Test the water first, bring alkalinity and then pH into range, shock to restore the sanitizer, rinse the filter, and run the jets with the cover open; most haze clears within a day.

sections.h2: Step 1: test before you add anything
sections.intro: Guessing is how a cloudy tub turns into a cloudy tub with too much acid in it. Dip a fresh test strip, or use a drop kit, and write down four numbers: sanitizer (free chlorine or bromine), pH, total alkalinity and, if your strip has it, calcium hardness.
sections.after: The free hot tub chemical calculator takes those readings, your tub size and the strength printed on your own bottles, and lists what to add in the right order.

sections.intro: Compare your numbers with the usual hot tub ranges. These follow CDC hot tub guidance for soaking and the common spa targets for balance.

head: Reading
Usual range
If it is outside the range
rows: Low chlorine lets bacteria and body oils cloud the water
Low bromine does the same; shocking reactivates spent bromide
High pH makes sanitizer weaker and lets calcium come out as haze
High alkalinity pushes pH up and keeps it there
Very high calcium plus high pH turns the water milky and leaves scale

sections.note: If every number is in range and the water is still cloudy, the filter or old water is the likely cause.

sections.h2: Step 2: fix it in this order
steps: Alkalinity first. It buffers pH, so correcting pH before alkalinity means doing it twice. Raise it with an alkalinity increaser or lower it with pH decreaser, following the label on your product.
Then pH. Bring it to about 7.4 to 7.6 with pH increaser or decreaser.
Then shock. A non chlorine or chlorine shock (whichever matches your sanitizer, per its label) burns off oils and restores the sanitizer level.
Rinse the filter with a garden hose, pleat by pleat, from top to bottom. Soak it in a filter cleaner if it is greasy.
Run the jets with the cover open for about 20 minutes after each addition, wait before adding the next product, and test again before anyone soaks.

list: Add a spa clarifier. It clumps fine particles so the filter can catch them. Follow its label and rinse the filter a day later.
Check the filter's age. Most spa filters need replacing about once a year, or sooner in a busy tub.
Think about the water's age. Most hot tubs need draining and refilling every three to four months. Water near its drain date is often faster to replace than to fix.
Look at what goes in with the bathers. Lotion, makeup, hair products and detergent in swimsuits all cloud water. A quick rinse before soaking helps.

paras: Cloudy water is hazy all the way through and usually means a chemistry or filtration problem. Foam sits on the surface and is usually soap, lotion or hair product, often with soft water (low calcium).
Foam often follows the same fix: test, balance, shock and rinse the filter. A spa defoamer knocks it down for the moment, but it comes back until the cause is gone.

sections.intro: TubTender is an iPhone app from Graysmith Labs that turns a test strip into a plan: tap the colors on your strip, scan the labels of the chemicals you own, and it lists how much of each to add for your tub size, in this same order, with a countdown until the water is safe to soak. Its cloudy and foamy water guides are free.
sections.note: TubTender is on the App Store for iPhone. The free hot tub calculator on this site runs the same engine in your browser.

sections.intro: Four things fix most cloudy tubs. Any brand works; what matters is the strength printed on the label, which the calculator asks for.
steps: Test strips that read sanitizer, pH and alkalinity: hot tub test strips on Amazon.
Spa shock to restore the sanitizer: dichlor chlorine granules for chlorine tubs, or spa shock for bromine for bromine tubs.
pH and alkalinity adjusters: pH decreaser, pH increaser and alkalinity increaser.
A filter cleaner for the monthly rinse: hot tub filter cleaner.

faq: Why is my hot tub water cloudy?
Usually low sanitizer, high pH or alkalinity, or a clogged filter. Old water with a lot of dissolved solids makes all of these worse.
Is it safe to use a cloudy hot tub?
It is best to wait. Cloudy water often means the sanitizer is too low to keep the water safe. Test, fix the sanitizer and pH, and soak once the readings are back in range.
How long does it take to clear cloudy hot tub water?
Most haze clears within 24 hours once the water is balanced, shocked and the filter is clean. If it is still cloudy after that, try a clarifier or drain and refill.
Will shock clear a cloudy hot tub?
Often, if low sanitizer or oils are the cause. Balance alkalinity and pH first so the shock works, and rinse the filter so it can catch what the shock breaks down.
Should I drain a cloudy hot tub?
Drain and refill if the water is near its drain date (typically three to four months), if calcium or dissolved solids are very high, or if balancing and shocking have not cleared it.

guides.title: How to Lower Hot Tub Alkalinity (and Keep pH Steady)
guides.description: Lower hot tub alkalinity: add pH decreaser until pH is about 7.2, then run the jets with the cover off so pH rises. Repeat daily until 80 to 120 ppm.
guides.h1: How to lower hot tub alkalinity
guides.answer: To lower hot tub alkalinity, add pH decreaser (dry acid) or muriatic acid until pH reads about 7.2, which uses up alkalinity, then run the jets with the cover off for 30 to 60 minutes so pH climbs back without the alkalinity returning. Retest the next day and repeat until total alkalinity sits between 80 and 120 ppm; most tubs get there in two to four rounds.

sections.h2: Why acid and air, not acid alone
paras: Total alkalinity is the water's buffer: it holds pH in place. Any acid you add lowers both pH and alkalinity at the same time, so there is no product that lowers alkalinity on its own.

The trick is the second half. Aeration (jets, air blower, cover off) lets dissolved carbon dioxide escape, and that raises pH without adding any alkalinity back. Acid down, air up, repeat: each round leaves alkalinity lower and pH where it started.

steps: Test first. Write down total alkalinity and pH. If alkalinity is 120 ppm or less, leave it alone and fix pH instead.

Work out the dose. The free hot tub calculator takes your readings, tub size and the strength on your bottle, and gives the amount of pH decreaser that brings pH to 7.2. Without it, follow the label and start with less than it says; you can always add more.

Add the acid with the circulation pump running and the air jets off, so it mixes without being aerated away. Pour dry acid into the water slowly, or dissolve it in a bucket of tub water first. Add muriatic acid to water, never water to acid, with gloves and eye protection.
Wait 20 minutes and retest pH. If it is still above 7.2, add a smaller second dose.
Aerate. Turn the jets and air blower on and leave the cover off for 30 to 60 minutes. pH rises; alkalinity stays down.
Retest the next day. Alkalinity still above 120 ppm? Repeat from step 2. Once it is in range, set pH to about 7.4 to 7.6 and shock as usual.

sections.intro: These are the common spa targets, the same ones the calculator and TubTender use.

head: Reading
Target
Why it matters
rows: Too high and pH keeps drifting up; too low and pH swings with every soak
High pH weakens chlorine and bromine and can cloud the water
Low enough to use up alkalinity, not so low that it bites skin or metal

sections.note: Do not soak while pH is below 7.2. Wait until aeration has brought it back into range.

list: Fill water. Many areas have hard, high alkalinity tap water, so every top up adds more. Test a glass of tap water once to know what you start with.
pH increaser (soda ash) and alkalinity increaser (baking soda) both add alkalinity. Using either to fix a low pH reading that was really a testing error is a common cause.
Liquid chlorine and bleach nudge pH up, which tempts more acid and more swings. Small, regular doses keep it steady.
Old water. After three to four months dissolved solids build up and balance gets harder. If alkalinity is far above 200 ppm and the water is near its drain date, a partial drain and refill is faster.
Lowering pH first and alkalinity later. Alkalinity pulls pH back up within a day, so you end up doing it twice. Fix alkalinity first, then pH.
Adding the whole label dose at once. Big doses overshoot pH into the 6s. Split it and retest.
Using vinegar. It barely moves alkalinity and adds organics the sanitizer has to burn off.
Running the air jets while the acid goes in. That raises pH again before the acid has used up any alkalinity.

When alkalinity is high it shows this same lower then aerate plan.

A pH decreaser (sodium bisulfate, also sold as dry acid): spa pH decreaser.

faq: How do I lower alkalinity in my hot tub?
Add pH decreaser or muriatic acid until pH is about 7.2, then run the jets with the cover off for 30 to 60 minutes so pH rises again. Retest the next day and repeat until alkalinity is 80 to 120 ppm.
Can I lower alkalinity without lowering pH?
Not with one product. Acid always lowers both. Aeration then raises pH back without adding alkalinity, so the pair of steps lowers alkalinity while pH ends where it began.
What is the right total alkalinity for a hot tub?
80 to 120 ppm for most hot tubs. Check your tub's manual, since some makers name a slightly different range.
How long does it take to lower hot tub alkalinity?
Usually two to four days, one round of acid and aeration per day, with a retest each morning. Very high readings may need a partial drain.
Should I fix alkalinity or pH first?
Alkalinity first. It buffers pH, so pH set before alkalinity drifts back within a day.
Is it safe to use the hot tub while lowering alkalinity?
Wait until pH is back to at least 7.2 and the sanitizer is in range. Low pH can sting eyes and skin.

guides.title: How Much Chlorine to Add to a Hot Tub (by Tub Size)
guides.description: How much chlorine to add to a hot tub: about 1¾ tsp of dichlor or 2½ fl oz of 6% bleach raises a 400 gallon tub by 3 ppm. Keep it at 3 to 10 ppm.
guides.h1: How much chlorine to add to a hot tub
guides.answer: For a typical 400 gallon hot tub, about 1¾ teaspoons (0.3 oz) of 56 percent dichlor granules, or about 2½ fl oz of 6 percent unscented bleach, raises free chlorine by 3 ppm, enough to take a reading of 1 ppm up to the 4 ppm target. As a rule of thumb, half a teaspoon of dichlor per 100 gallons adds about 3.5 ppm. Keep free chlorine between 3 and 10 ppm, the range CDC guidance gives for hot tubs, and retest 20 minutes after each dose.

sections.h2: How much to add, by tub size
sections.intro: Amounts to raise free chlorine by 3 ppm, for example from 1 ppm to 4 ppm. They come from the same chemistry engine as the free hot tub calculator and the TubTender app, and assume dichlor at 56 percent available chlorine and bleach at the strength shown.
sections.note: Need a different rise? Scale it: 1 ppm is a third of the amount shown. Products vary, so check the strength on your label or enter it in the calculator for an exact dose.
sections.after: A typical label shock dose is about 1 teaspoon of dichlor per 100 gallons, which adds roughly 7 ppm. Use it after a busy soak, then wait until a retest shows 10 ppm or less before anyone gets in.

steps: Test first with a strip or drop kit and write down free chlorine and pH. If pH is above 7.8, lower it first: chlorine is much weaker at high pH.
Know your tub's volume in gallons. It is in the manual or on the maker's site; most two to six seat tubs hold 250 to 600 gallons.
Read the strength on your product's label: the percent of available chlorine for granules, or the percent of sodium hypochlorite for bleach.
Work out the dose with the free hot tub calculator, or use the table above. Start with a little less than you think; you can always add more.
Add it with the cover open and the jets running. Sprinkle granules slowly across the water, or pour bleach in front of a jet.
Wait 20 minutes with the jets on, then retest. Soak only when free chlorine reads 3 to 10 ppm and pH 7.2 to 7.8.

list: Before each soak: test, and top up if free chlorine is under 3 ppm.
After each soak: bodies, lotion and sweat use chlorine up fast in hot water, so a small dose after use keeps the next reading in range.
At least two or three times a week when the tub sits unused, because heat and the jets slowly burn chlorine off.
After a heavy use day or a party: a full shock dose, then wait for it to drop to 10 ppm or less before soaking.

paras: Both work. Dichlor granules (sodium dichloroisocyanurate, sold as spa shock or chlorinating granules) store well and barely move pH, but each dose also adds stabilizer (cyanuric acid), about 0.9 ppm for every 1 ppm of chlorine. Stabilizer builds up over weeks and makes chlorine slower; once it passes about 50 ppm, drain part of the water and refill.

Plain unscented bleach adds no stabilizer, costs little and is easy to measure, but it nudges pH up a little and loses strength as it ages, so buy it fresh and use the regular kind, not splashless or scented. Many owners use dichlor for daily doses and switch to bleach for a while when stabilizer gets high.
Skip chlorine pucks made for pools (trichlor): they are very acidic and build stabilizer quickly. Calcium hypochlorite raises calcium and can cloud spa water.
sections.note: CDC recommends not using chlorine products that contain cyanuric acid, dichlor included, in hot tubs, because the stabilizer slows disinfection (CDC home hot tub page). Many home owners and spa brands still use dichlor. To follow CDC, use plain unscented bleach.
sections.after: Still choosing a sanitizer? See bromine vs chlorine for a hot tub.

list: Reading total chlorine instead of free chlorine. Free chlorine is the part that sanitizes; dose from that number.
Adding chlorine to water with pH above 7.8. At pH 8 only about a quarter of free chlorine is in its strong form, against about half at 7.5.
Closing the cover right after a dose. Leave it open with the jets on for 20 minutes so gases escape.
Getting in above 10 ppm. High chlorine irritates skin, eyes and lungs; wait for it to come down.
Guessing the dose from a pool chart. Hot tubs are small, so pool amounts overshoot badly.

faq: How much chlorine do I put in my hot tub?
Enough to keep free chlorine between 3 and 10 ppm. For a 400 gallon tub, about 1¾ teaspoons of 56 percent dichlor granules or about 2½ fl oz of 6 percent bleach raises it by 3 ppm.
How much chlorine per 100 gallons in a hot tub?
Half a teaspoon of 56 percent dichlor granules per 100 gallons raises free chlorine by about 3.5 ppm. A full teaspoon per 100 gallons, the usual shock dose, adds about 7 ppm.
What should the chlorine level be in a hot tub?
Free chlorine 3 to 10 ppm, with pH 7.2 to 7.8. Those are the ranges in CDC hot tub guidance.
Can I use regular bleach in my hot tub?
Yes, plain unscented bleach works. Check its strength on the label (often 6 or 8.25 percent), dose by that, and avoid scented or splashless bleach.
How long after adding chlorine can I get in the hot tub?
Usually about 20 minutes with the jets running, once a retest shows free chlorine at 10 ppm or less and pH between 7.2 and 7.8.
Why does my hot tub chlorine keep dropping?
Heat, jets and bathers use it up quickly. High pH, too much stabilizer or old water also make it fade faster. Test before each soak and dose after use.

guides.title: Hot Tub pH Too High? How to Lower It Safely
guides.description: Hot tub pH too high: check alkalinity first, then add pH decreaser with the pump on. About 2¾ tsp takes a 400 gallon tub from pH 8.0 to 7.5.
guides.h1: Hot tub pH too high? How to lower it
guides.answer: When hot tub pH reads above 7.8, check total alkalinity first: if it is above 120 ppm, lower alkalinity instead, or pH will climb straight back. If alkalinity is in range, add pH decreaser (dry acid) with the pump running and the air jets off. For a 400 gallon tub at pH 8.0 with alkalinity at 90 ppm, about 2¾ teaspoons (0.5 oz) brings it to about 7.5; add half, wait 20 minutes, retest, then add the rest if needed.

sections.h2: How much pH decreaser to add
sections.intro: Amounts to bring pH down to about 7.5 with total alkalinity at 90 ppm. They come from the same chemistry engine as the free hot tub calculator and the TubTender app, for dry acid (sodium bisulfate, 93 percent) and muriatic acid (31.45 percent).
sections.note: Higher alkalinity needs more acid for the same change. Strip readings are coarse, so split every dose in half and retest between halves.

steps: Test total alkalinity and pH. Alkalinity above 120 ppm? Follow how to lower hot tub alkalinity instead; it brings pH down along the way.
Work out the dose with the free hot tub calculator or the table above, using the strength on your label.
Turn the circulation pump on and the air jets and blower off. Air raises pH, so it would undo part of the dose.
Add half the dose. Pour dry acid slowly over the water or dissolve it in a bucket of tub water first. Add muriatic acid to water, never water to acid, with gloves and eye protection.
Wait 20 minutes and retest. Still above 7.8? Add the second half and retest again.
Once pH reads 7.2 to 7.8, check sanitizer and top it up if it is low. High pH may have let it fade.

list: Jets and the air blower. Aeration lets carbon dioxide escape, and pH rises a little every time the tub runs. A slow upward drift is normal.
High total alkalinity. It pushes pH up and resists every dose. Fix it first.
Bleach and pH increaser. Liquid chlorine nudges pH up, and an extra scoop of soda ash after a misread strip is a common cause.
Fresh fill water. Many areas have tap water at pH 8 or higher, so a new fill often needs a first dose.

sections.intro: Target pH is 7.2 to 7.8, the range in CDC hot tub guidance. Above it:
list: Chlorine and bromine get much weaker. At pH 8 only about a quarter of free chlorine is in its strong form, against about half at 7.5.
Calcium comes out of the water as scale on the shell, jets and heater.
The water turns cloudy and can leave skin itchy or dry. See cloudy hot tub water if it looks hazy.
Dumping in the whole label dose at once. Big doses overshoot pH below 7.2, which stings eyes and wears on the heater.
Running the air jets while the acid goes in. That raises pH again before the acid has done its work.
Using vinegar or lemon juice. They barely move pH in a hot tub and add organics the sanitizer has to burn off.
Retesting right away. Give it 20 minutes of circulation or the reading will not be settled.

faq: How do I lower the pH in my hot tub?
Add pH decreaser (dry acid) or muriatic acid with the pump running and the air jets off. Add half the dose, wait 20 minutes, retest, then add the rest if pH is still above 7.8.
What happens if hot tub pH is too high?
Chlorine and bromine work much less well, scale forms on the shell and heater, and the water can turn cloudy and dry out skin.
Is it safe to use a hot tub with high pH?
It is better to wait. Above 7.8 the sanitizer is weak, so germs are not killed as fast. Lower pH to 7.2 to 7.8 first.
Why does my hot tub pH keep rising?
Aeration from the jets raises pH a little every day. High alkalinity, bleach and high pH tap water make it rise faster.
Should I lower alkalinity or pH first?
Alkalinity first when it is above 120 ppm. Lowering it brings pH down too, and pH set before alkalinity drifts back within a day.
Can I use vinegar to lower hot tub pH?
No. It barely moves pH in a hot tub and adds organics the sanitizer has to burn off. Use a spa pH decreaser.

guides.title: How Often to Test Hot Tub Water: A Simple Schedule
guides.description: Test hot tub sanitizer and pH two to three times a week and before every soak after a busy day, alkalinity weekly, calcium monthly. Full schedule inside.
guides.h1: How often to test hot tub water
guides.answer: Test sanitizer (chlorine or bromine) and pH at least two to three times a week in a home hot tub, and before you soak after heavy use, a party or a few days away. Test total alkalinity once a week and calcium hardness once a month and after every refill. Rinse the filter about every two weeks and drain and refill every three to four months, sooner when the tub is used every day.

sections.intro: A schedule for a home tub with one to four regular soakers. The target ranges come from the same chemistry engine as the free hot tub calculator and the TubTender app.

head: What
How often
Target
rows: 2 to 3 times a week, and before soaking after heavy use
2 to 3 times a week, and before soaking after heavy use
2 to 3 times a week, with the sanitizer
Once a month and after every refill
Hose it off, pleat by pleat
Every 3 to 4 months, sooner with daily use

sections.note: Test more often in the first week after a refill, after a big group soak and after rain gets in. Chemistry moves fastest then.

list: Before the first soak after a party or several people in a row. Every soaker uses up sanitizer.
When the water looks hazy or smells strong of chemicals. That smell usually means used up chlorine, not too much. See cloudy hot tub water.
After you add any chemical. Wait 20 minutes with the pump running, then retest before adding more.
After a few days away or a power cut. Sanitizer fades fast in hot water with the cover on and no one adding any.
When skin itches or eyes sting. pH is often the cause; see hot tub pH too high.

sections.h2: How to test hot tub water in a minute
steps: Run the pump for a few minutes so the water is mixed, then turn the jets off.
Dip a strip elbow deep, away from the jets and any floating dispenser, for the time on the bottle (usually one or two seconds).
Hold it flat and compare the colors to the chart within about 15 seconds. Colors keep changing after that.
Fix things in order: alkalinity first, then pH, then sanitizer. The free hot tub calculator gives the amount for each from your readings and tub size.
Write the readings down, or log them in an app, so you can see which way the water is drifting.

sections.h2: How often to drain a hot tub
sections.intro: A common rule is gallons divided by 3, divided by the number of people who soak on an average day, gives the days between refills. TubTender uses that rule and keeps the result between two weeks and about four months.
sections.note: Drain sooner if the water stays cloudy or foamy after balancing, or if sanitizer will not hold. Old water is full of dissolved solids that no dose can fix.

list: Testing only when the water looks wrong. By then sanitizer has usually been low for days.
Using old strips. A bottle that has been open for months or kept in a humid spot reads wrong; keep the lid tight and replace it once it passes the date on the label.
Reading the strip late. A strip read a minute after dipping looks stronger than the water is.
Adjusting everything at once. Change one thing, circulate, retest, then move to the next.

sections.h2: A faster way to keep up
sections.intro: TubTender is an iPhone app from Graysmith Labs that turns a test strip into a plan: tap the colors on your strip, scan the labels of the chemicals you own, and it lists how much of each to add for your tub size, in the right order, with a countdown until the water is safe to soak. Free reminders nudge you to test every three days, rinse the filter every two weeks and drain when the tub is due, and the tub on Home changes mood with your latest test and how long it has been since you checked.
sections.note: TubTender is on the App Store for iPhone. The free hot tub calculator on this site runs the same engine in your browser.

sections.intro: Any brand works; what matters is that the strips read your sanitizer and the chemicals list their strength on the label.
steps: Test strips that read your sanitizer, pH and alkalinity: hot tub test strips on Amazon.
Your sanitizer: spa chlorine granules or bromine tablets. Not sure which? See bromine vs chlorine.
A filter cleaner for the rinse every two weeks: hot tub filter cleaner.
sections.note: As an Amazon Associate, Graysmith Labs earns from qualifying purchases. The links search Amazon for each product type; none of them changes how much to add.

faq: How often should I test my hot tub water?
Test chlorine or bromine and pH two to three times a week, and before soaking after heavy use. Test alkalinity weekly and calcium hardness monthly and after each refill.
Should I test hot tub water before every use?
If several people soak or the tub sat unused for a few days, yes. Sanitizer fades fast in hot water, and a quick strip takes under a minute.
How often should I test a new hot tub fill?
Every day for the first week. Fresh water moves quickly while you bring alkalinity, pH, calcium and sanitizer into range.
How often should I drain my hot tub?
Every three to four months for most home tubs. Divide the gallons by 3, then by the number of daily soakers, for the days between refills.
Are test strips accurate enough?
Yes for routine checks, if they are fresh, kept dry and read within about 15 seconds. Use a drop kit to double check a strange reading.

guides.title: Bromine vs Chlorine for a Hot Tub: Which to Use
guides.description: Bromine holds steadier in hot water and smells less; chlorine costs less and works faster. Levels, cost, smell, sunlight and how to switch safely.
guides.h1: Bromine vs chlorine for a hot tub
guides.answer: Choose bromine if you want a level that holds steadily in hot water with a floater and less smell; choose chlorine if you want the cheaper, faster option and do not mind dosing after each soak. Both keep a hot tub clean when the level is right: bromine 4 to 8 ppm or free chlorine 3 to 10 ppm, with pH at 7.2 to 7.8. Never mix the two products or put them in the same feeder, and drain the tub before changing from one to the other.

sections.h2: Bromine and chlorine side by side
sections.intro: The levels are the ranges in CDC hot tub guidance, which the free hot tub calculator and the TubTender app also use.

head: Bromine
Chlorine
rows: Breaks down, but slower than bromine
Stronger, mostly from used up chlorine
Keep a floater filled, shock to refresh
Dose by hand, often after each soak

sections.note: Skin reactions vary. Some people find one gentler than the other, but pH out of range bothers skin with either.

list: Bromine suits a tub that stays hot, has its cover on and is used most days, or anyone who would rather fill a floater than dose by hand.
Chlorine suits a tub in the open sun, occasional use, frequent refills or a tight budget.
Check the manual first. Some covers, heaters and salt systems are made for one of them, and the warranty may say so.
If someone has had a reaction to pool water, ask a doctor before choosing. Bromine is not a cure for a chlorine allergy.

sections.h2: How each one works day to day
paras: Chlorine acts on its own. You add granules or bleach, test, and add more as it is used up. Used up chlorine is what smells. See how much chlorine to add to a hot tub for amounts by tub size.

Bromine works from a reserve. After a fill you add sodium bromide as its label says, then keep tablets in a floater. When the reading falls, a chlorine based shock turns the used bromide in the water back into bromine. That is why a small dose goes a long way: 1 ppm of chlorine makes about 2.25 ppm of bromine. A zero reading just after a refill usually means the reserve has not been added yet.
Using shock to refresh a bromine tub is normal. Mixing the dry products is not: never put bromine and chlorine in the same container, scoop or feeder.

sections.intro: To raise bromine by 3 ppm, for example from 2 to 5 ppm, in a tub that already has its bromide reserve. Worked out with the formula in the TubTender engine, for 56 percent dichlor and 6 percent bleach. Use one or the other, not both.
sections.note: Dichlor adds stabilizer (cyanuric acid). CDC recommends not using products that contain it in hot tubs (CDC home hot tub page), so plain unscented bleach is the choice that follows CDC. Products vary; enter the strength on your label in the calculator.

sections.h2: How to switch from one to the other
steps: Drain the tub. Bromide stays in the water, so chlorine added to it just makes more bromine.
Clean the shell, rinse or replace the filter, and use a new floater if the old one held the other product.
Refill and balance alkalinity first, then pH, then calcium.
For bromine, add the bromide reserve as its label says, then shock. For chlorine, add the first dose.
Run the jets with the cover open for 20 minutes, test, and soak once the level and pH are in range.
Store the old product away from the new one, dry and sealed.

list: Adding trichlor pool tablets to a hot tub floater. They are very acidic and look much like bromine tablets.
Reading a bromine tub on the chlorine scale. Use the bromine colors on the strip.
Relying on tablets alone. They hold a level; shock brings a low one back quickly.
Going by smell. Test two or three times a week at least; CDC advises twice a day. See how often to test hot tub water.

sections.h2: Let the app do the math
sections.intro: TubTender is an iPhone app from Graysmith Labs that works with bromine and chlorine tubs. Tap the colors on your strip, scan the labels of the chemicals you own, and it lists how much of each to add for your tub size, in order. Bromine tubs get shock doses and a floater reminder.
sections.note: TubTender is on the App Store for iPhone. The free hot tub calculator on this site runs the same engine in your browser.

sections.intro: Any brand works. Buy for the sanitizer you picked and check the label.
steps: Bromine tub: bromine tablets, a floater and sodium bromide for refills.
Chlorine tub: spa chlorine granules or plain unscented bleach.
Both: test strips that read your sanitizer.
sections.note: As an Amazon Associate, Graysmith Labs earns from qualifying purchases. The links search Amazon for each product type; none of them changes how much to add.

faq: Is bromine or chlorine better for a hot tub?
Bromine is steadier in hot water and smells less. Chlorine costs less, works faster and lasts better in sun. Either is fine if you keep it in range.
Can I switch from chlorine to bromine without draining?
Drain first. Swim University gives the same advice: drain, clean and refill before adding the new sanitizer. Going from bromine to chlorine always needs it, because bromide stays in the water.
Can you use chlorine shock in a bromine hot tub?
Yes. A chlorine based shock turns used bromide back into bromine. Follow the label, and never mix the dry products together.
What level should bromine be in a hot tub?
4 to 8 ppm, with pH 7.2 to 7.8. Chlorine should be 3 to 10 ppm. TubTender aims for 5 ppm bromine.
Is bromine better for sensitive skin?
Some people find it gentler, but reactions vary and pH out of range irritates skin with either. Ask a doctor if you have had a reaction.

guides.title: Sleep Sounds That Work Offline on a Plane (iPhone)
guides.description: Yes, you can play sleep sounds offline on a plane. Use an app whose sounds ship inside it, test in airplane mode before you fly, and set a sleep timer.
guides.h1: Sleep sounds that work offline on a plane
guides.answer: Yes: a sleep sounds app plays on a plane as long as its sounds are stored on your phone, so pick one whose sounds ship inside the app (Drift, for example) or download your sounds before you board, and test it in airplane mode at home. Steady sounds like fan or a deep white noise mask engine roar best, at the lowest volume that covers it.

sections.h2: Test it in airplane mode before you fly
sections.intro: Many sleep apps stream their sounds or keep most of them online. Find out on the ground, not at 35,000 feet.
steps: Open Control Center and turn on Airplane Mode. Turn WiFi off too, because planes often let you turn it back on.
Open your sleep app and play each sound you plan to use.
Lock the screen and wait a minute. The sound should keep playing.
Set the sleep timer and make sure it still counts down offline.
If a sound will not play, it is streamed. Download it inside the app, or use an app whose sounds are built in.

sections.h2: Which sounds cover engine noise best
paras: Cabin noise is a steady low roar, so a steady sound with plenty of low end covers it best. Fan and a deep white noise (often called brown noise) blend into the engine instead of fighting it. Rain and ocean change over time, which some people find more relaxing but which masks less.
Keep the volume low. Headphones on a plane are easy to turn up too far, and a sound only needs to be slightly louder than the noise you are covering.

list: Charge your phone and headphones, or pack a short cable.
Pick one sound and a sleep timer of about an hour so the app stops on its own.
Wired headphones or earbuds that fit well block more noise than loose ones. Noise cancelling headphones plus a quiet sound work better than either alone.
Turn on Do Not Disturb or a Sleep focus so notifications do not wake you when you land.

sections.h2: Apps whose sounds ship inside compared with streamed sounds

head: Sounds built into the app
Streamed or downloadable sounds
rows: Only the sounds you downloaded first
Calm, BetterSleep and most large libraries (download first)

sections.after: The free white noise generator on this site plays in a browser, but it needs a connection to load, so use an app on the plane.

sections.intro: Drift is a free white noise and sleep sounds app for iPhone and iPad from Graysmith Labs. Every sound ships inside the app, so it plays the same in airplane mode as at home, and it keeps playing with the screen locked.
steps: Pick a sound. White noise, rain, ocean, stream and fan are free.
Set the sleep timer: 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour or 2 hours. Turn on wind down if you want it to fade out at the end.
Lock your phone. Sleep mode keeps the screen dark if you leave it open.
sections.note: Premium is $1.99 a month for thirteen more sounds and no ads, and eligible new subscribers get a free week.

faq: Do sleep sound apps work in airplane mode?
Only if the sounds are stored on your phone. Apps that stream need you to download sounds first. Drift's sounds ship inside the app, so it works in airplane mode with nothing to prepare.
What is the best sound to sleep on a plane?
A steady sound with low tones, such as fan or a deep white noise, blends into engine noise better than changing sounds like waves.
Will the sound keep playing when my iPhone locks?
In apps that support background audio, yes. Test it at home by locking the screen for a minute before you rely on it in the air.
Is white noise safe to listen to on a long flight?
Keep the volume at the lowest level that covers the cabin noise and use a sleep timer so it does not play all flight.

guides.title: Brown Noise for Sleep: What It Is and How to Use It (iPhone)
guides.description: Brown noise is a deep, soft rumble with more low tones than white noise. How it differs, who it suits, and how to play it free all night on iPhone.
guides.h1: Brown noise for sleep: what it is and how to use it
guides.answer: Brown noise is random sound with most of its energy in the low tones, so it sounds like a deep, soft rumble (a waterfall or a strong wind far away) instead of the bright hiss of white noise. Many light sleepers find it easier to fall asleep to, and you can play it free all night on an iPhone with a white noise app such as Drift, at the lowest volume that covers the noise around you.

sections.h2: Brown, white, pink and green noise compared
sections.intro: All four are steady random sound. What changes is how the energy is spread between low and high tones, which changes how it feels to fall asleep to.

head: Sounds like
Good for
rows: A bright hiss, like an untuned radio
Covering voices and sharp sounds in a noisy room
A softer, balanced static, like steady rain
People who find white noise too sharp
A deep rumble, like a waterfall or distant thunder
Light sleepers, low hums, traffic and loud neighbors
A mellow hush in the middle tones
A calm background that is neither bright nor deep

sections.after: You can hear each one side by side in the free white noise generator on this site before you pick one for the night.

sections.h2: Why some people sleep better with brown noise
paras: Most of the sounds that wake people at night are low: traffic, a neighbor's music, an air conditioner, a partner snoring. A sound with plenty of low end blends with them, so the brain stops noticing the change when they start and stop. Brown noise also lacks the high hiss of white noise, which many people describe as tiring after an hour.

Research on colored noise and sleep is still small, and no noise is a treatment for insomnia. The honest advice is to try two or three nights each of brown and white noise and keep the one you fall asleep to faster.

sections.h2: How to play brown noise all night on an iPhone
steps: Install a sleep sounds app whose sounds play with the screen locked and work offline, so a weak signal never stops it at 3 AM.
Pick Brown Noise and set the volume just loud enough to cover the noise around you, then turn it down a step.
Put the phone a little away from your head, on a nightstand or the floor, instead of under the pillow.
Choose no timer if you wake when the sound stops, or a timer of an hour or two with a fade out if you only need help falling asleep.
Lock the phone and turn on a Sleep focus so notifications do not light the screen.

list: Aim for about the level of a quiet shower or softer. If you have to raise your voice over it, it is too loud.
Speakers are kinder than earbuds for a whole night. If you need earbuds, use soft sleep earbuds and a low volume.
For a baby, keep the speaker across the room, well away from the crib, and keep it quiet. Ask your pediatrician if you are unsure.
Check Settings, Sounds and Haptics, Headphone Safety on an iPhone to see how loud your listening has been.

sections.h2: Drift: free brown noise that plays until morning
sections.intro: Drift is a white noise and sleep sounds app for iPhone and iPad from Graysmith Labs. Brown Noise is free for everyone, with no time limit, and every sound loops without a gap, keeps playing with the screen locked and works offline.
steps: Open Drift and tap Brown Noise. White Noise, Rain, Ocean, Stream, Fan and the 432 Hz tone are free too.
Leave the timer off to play all night, or pick 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour or 2 hours and turn on wind down to fade it out.
Lock your phone, or leave Sleep mode open to keep the screen dark.
sections.note: Premium is $1.99 a month for pink and green noise, thirteen more sounds and no ads, and eligible new subscribers get a free week.

faq: Is brown noise better than white noise for sleep?

Neither is better for everyone. Brown noise is deeper and softer, so many light sleepers and people bothered by low sounds like traffic prefer it; white noise covers voices and sharp sounds better. Try each for a few nights.
Is it safe to sleep with brown noise on all night?

For most adults, yes, at a low volume from a speaker a little away from your head. Keep it at the level of a quiet shower or softer, and use a timer with a fade out if you only need help falling asleep.
What does brown noise sound like?
A deep, steady rumble, like a waterfall, a strong wind far away or the inside of an airplane cabin, with none of the hiss of white noise.
Can I play brown noise on my iPhone for free?

Yes. Drift plays Brown Noise free with no time limit, keeps playing with the screen locked and works offline. iPhone also has a built in Background Sounds setting under Accessibility, Audio and Visual, though it has fewer choices and no sleep timer.
Why is it called brown noise?
It is named after Brownian motion, the random movement of particles, not the color brown. Its energy falls as the pitch rises, which is why it sounds so deep.

guides.title: How to Improve Reaction Time: What Works, 10 Minutes a Day
guides.description: How to improve reaction time: short daily practice on fast decisions, enough sleep and fewer distractions. Test a baseline, train, retest weekly.
guides.h1: How to improve your reaction time
guides.answer: You can improve your reaction time with short daily practice on tasks that ask for fast decisions, enough sleep, and fewer distractions while you play or drive. Practice mostly makes you faster at the kind of task you practice, so train something close to what you want to be quick at, take a baseline with a free reaction time test, and retest once a week on the same device.

sections.intro: There are two kinds, and they train differently.

head: Kind
Example
What changes it
rows: Tap when a box turns green
Mostly alertness, sleep and your device. Most adults land about 250 to 300 ms in a tap test, and practice shaves off a little
Find the right shape among several and tap it
Slower, and slower again with more options to choose from. This is where practice pays off most, because you learn to spot the target faster

sections.after: Sports, driving and games are almost all choice reactions: you have to notice, decide and then move. That is why drills that make you pick the right target train more of what matters than a single go signal.

list: Short, daily practice. Ten focused minutes a day beats an hour once a week, and speed gains come from repetition of the same kind of decision.
Practice that gets harder. Once a drill feels easy, shrink the time limit or add more options to choose from, so you keep working at the edge of your speed.
Sleep. Being short on sleep slows reactions and causes more misses; a tired attempt is often 30 to 50 ms slower on a tap test.
Fewer distractions. Talking, notifications and a phone in hand while driving all slow how fast you notice a change.

Fast paced games. Studies of action video game players, starting with Green and Bavelier in Nature in 2003, found better visual attention than in non players, and short training sessions improved it in some people.
Being warm and ready. A quick warm up and a relaxed, ready hand (finger hovering, not resting) help in the moment.

steps: Take a baseline. Do five rounds of the free reaction time test and write down your average, not your best.
Two minutes of simple reaction. A few more rounds of the test, focusing on a hovering finger and watching the whole box.
Six minutes of choice reaction. Play a game that makes you find and tap a target fast, and let it get harder as you improve.
Two minutes of review. Note your average and anything that slowed you down: tiredness, distraction, a slow screen.
Retest once a week, at the same time of day and on the same device, so the comparison is fair.

list: Guessing early. Jumping before the signal makes a test score look better and teaches nothing useful.
Changing devices between tests. Screens and touch sensors each add their own delay, often a few tens of milliseconds.
Supplements sold for reflexes. Caffeine can help a little for a while; most other claims have weak evidence.
sections.note: This guide is for fun and training. It is not medical advice. If your reactions suddenly get slower, see a doctor.

sections.h2: Train it in one minute rounds
sections.intro: BlitzTap is a free iPhone and iPad game from Graysmith Labs built for choice reaction practice: a target shape appears and you tap its match in a grid before the timer runs out. As your score climbs the grid grows, distractors multiply and the timer shrinks to about a second by Tier 4, so it keeps you at the edge of your speed.
sections.note: Classic, Time Attack (60 seconds), Zen and a Daily Challenge with the same 30 targets for every player. Personal bests are tracked, so you can see the change week to week.

faq: How can I improve my reaction time?
Practice short daily sessions on tasks that need fast decisions, make them harder as you improve, sleep enough and cut distractions. Measure a baseline and retest weekly on the same device.
What is a good reaction time?
In a tap or click test, most adults average about 250 to 300 milliseconds. Under 250 ms is quick and under 200 ms is very fast.
Can you really train reaction time?
Yes, mostly for the kind of task you practice. Choice reactions, where you have to find the right target first, improve the most with practice.
How long does it take to improve reaction time?
Many people see their averages drop within a couple of weeks of daily practice. Big jumps usually come from fixing sleep or distraction rather than drills alone.
Do video games improve reaction time?
Fast paced games that make you spot and respond to targets have been linked with better visual attention in studies. Short daily sessions work better than long ones.
What slows reaction time down?
Too little sleep, distraction, alcohol, some medicines, and the device itself, since screens and touch sensors each add a little delay.

guides.title: Sign One Document Free Without a DocuSign Account
guides.description: Need to sign just one document? Three free ways to sign a PDF on iPhone with no DocuSign account or subscription, and when DocuSign still fits.
guides.h1: How to sign one document for free without DocuSign
guides.answer: If someone sent you a DocuSign link, you can sign it for free without creating an account: open the email, tap Review Document and follow the prompts. If you only have a PDF or a paper form to sign yourself, you do not need DocuSign at all: sign it with Markup in the iPhone Files app, or with a signing app such as SignSnap, which needs no account and keeps the document on your phone.

sections.h2: First: did someone send you a DocuSign link?
sections.intro: Signing a document someone sent you through DocuSign is always free. The sender pays; you do not need an account or the app.
steps: Open the email from DocuSign and tap Review Document.
Agree to use electronic records and signatures when it asks.
Tap each yellow tag to place your signature, initials or date. The first time, DocuSign asks you to adopt a signature: pick a style or draw one.
Tap Finish. You can download a copy without signing up.
sections.note: Only make an account if you want to send documents to other people for signature. That is the part DocuSign charges for.

sections.h2: Signing a PDF yourself: Markup in Files (free, built in)
sections.intro: For a PDF that is already on your iPhone, the Files app signs it with nothing to install.
steps: In Mail, tap the attachment, tap the share button and choose Save to Files.
Open the PDF in Files and tap the Markup button (a pen tip inside a circle).
Tap the plus button, choose Add Signature, sign with your finger and tap Done.
Drag the signature onto the line, resize it, then tap Done and share the PDF back.
sections.after: The full step by step version is in how to sign a PDF on iPhone.

sections.h2: Paper forms and frequent signing: SignSnap
sections.intro: SignSnap is an iPhone and iPad app from Graysmith Labs made only for signing your own documents. It suits paper forms, and people who sign often and want the date stamped beside the signature.
steps: Scan the page with the camera (the scanner finds the edges and straightens it) or import the PDF from Files or Photos.
Draw your signature with your finger, or type your name and pick a script font. It is saved for next time.
Place it on the line, pinch to resize and tap Date to stamp today's date.
Share the signed PDF to Mail, Messages or AirDrop.
sections.note: No account and no uploads. The first 2 signed documents are free, then one short ad unlocks one more signing; Premium (weekly, monthly or yearly, with a free week for new subscribers) removes the limit and the ads.

head: DocuSign (as signer)
Markup in Files
SignSnap
rows: 2 documents free, then an ad or Premium
Date tag if the sender added one

sections.after: Need a signature image for a Word file or a website form instead? The free signature maker draws or types one and downloads a transparent PNG, with nothing uploaded.

sections.h2: Is it legally valid without DocuSign?
paras: In the United States, the ESIGN Act and the state laws based on UETA generally treat an electronic signature as valid whatever tool made it, as long as both sides agree to sign electronically. DocuSign adds an audit trail of who signed and when, which matters most for high value contracts.

Some documents need more, such as wills, certain court papers and anything that must be notarized. When unsure, ask whoever sent the document whether a signed PDF is acceptable. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq: Can I sign a DocuSign document without an account?
Yes. Signing a document someone sent you through DocuSign is free and needs no account: open the email, tap Review Document, place your signature and tap Finish.
What is a free alternative to DocuSign for one document?
To sign a PDF yourself, use Markup in the iPhone Files app, which is built in, or a signing app such as SignSnap, whose first 2 signed documents are free with no account.
Do I need DocuSign to sign a PDF on my phone?
No. Any PDF can be signed with Markup in the Files app or with a signing app, then emailed back.
Can SignSnap send a document to someone else to sign?
No. SignSnap is for signing your own documents. To collect signatures from other people, use a service built for that, such as DocuSign.

guides.title: How to Put Affirmations on Your iPhone Lock Screen
guides.description: Put affirmations on your iPhone Lock Screen for free with a wallpaper or a daily reminder, or add a widget that shows a new affirmation through the day.
guides.h1: How do I put affirmations on my iPhone lock screen?
guides.answer: The free way is to make a wallpaper with your affirmation on it and set it as your Lock Screen, or to add a daily repeating reminder whose text is your affirmation so it appears on the Lock Screen each morning. If you want a different affirmation through the day without making images, add a Lock Screen widget from an affirmations app such as SayBright (today's affirmation is free; changing through the day is Premium).

sections.intro: This takes about two minutes and needs no app.
steps: Write your affirmation in large text: in Notes, in a photo editor, or on paper you photograph. Short lines read best, for example I am calm and capable.
Take a screenshot or a photo of it and crop it in Photos so the words sit in the middle of the frame, below where the clock will be.
Open Settings, tap Wallpaper, then Add New Wallpaper, and choose Photos.
Pick your image, move it so the clock does not cover the words, and tap Add.
Choose Set as Wallpaper Pair, or Customize Home Screen if you want a different home screen.

sections.h2: Free method 2: a daily reminder that says it for you
sections.intro: A notification shows on the Lock Screen, so a repeating reminder puts the words in front of you at the time you choose.
steps: Open the Reminders app and tap New Reminder.
Type your affirmation as the reminder's title.
Tap the details button, turn on Date and Time, and pick the time you want to see it.
Tap Repeat and choose Daily, then tap Done.
Each day the affirmation appears on your Lock Screen. Mark it done after you read it out loud, and it comes back tomorrow.

sections.h2: With an app: a Lock Screen widget
paras: A wallpaper says the same thing every day. An affirmations app widget changes through the day, so the words do not fade into the background. To add one, touch and hold the Lock Screen, tap Customize, tap Lock Screen, tap the area below the clock and pick the app's widget.

SayBright is one option: its free plan gives five affirmations a day, the whole Confidence category, a daily reminder, streaks and free Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets with today's affirmation, and Premium ($0.99 a month or $9.99 a year) adds widgets that change all day, every category and recordings in your own voice. Other affirmation apps such as I am and ThinkUp also offer widgets, so pick the one whose words sound like you.

list: Keep it short and in the present tense: I handle hard things, not I will be less anxious.
Read it out loud once when you first see it. Saying it is what turns a wallpaper into a habit.
Change it every week or two so your eyes do not skip over it.
Pair it with something you already do, like the first time you unlock your phone in the morning.

faq: How do I put affirmations on my iPhone lock screen for free?

Make an image with your affirmation, then open Settings, Wallpaper, Add New Wallpaper, Photos, and set it as your Lock Screen. Or create a daily repeating reminder in Reminders whose title is your affirmation.
Is there an affirmation widget for the iPhone lock screen?

Yes. Several affirmation apps offer Lock Screen widgets. SayBright's Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets show today's affirmation for free; Premium, $0.99 a month or $9.99 a year, makes them change all day. Its free plan gives five affirmations a day.
How do I add a widget to my iPhone lock screen?
Touch and hold the Lock Screen, tap Customize, tap Lock Screen, then tap the area below the clock and choose a widget. Tap Done to save.

guides.title: How to Start a Daily Affirmation Habit That Sticks
guides.description: Start a daily affirmation habit: pick a fixed moment, say three to five believable affirmations out loud, and use a reminder and a streak to keep it going.
guides.h1: How to start a daily affirmation habit
guides.answer: To start a daily affirmation habit, tie it to something you already do every day, such as right after you wake up or brush your teeth, and say three to five short affirmations out loud at that moment. Pick ones you can believe, keep them in the present tense, and use a reminder and a simple streak so a missed day is easy to notice and easy to restart.

steps: Pick your anchor. Choose one thing you already do daily, like making coffee or brushing your teeth. Your affirmations come right after it.

Choose three to five affirmations. Start with one area you want more of, such as confidence or calm. Keep them short and believable: "I can handle today one step at a time" lands better than a claim you do not believe yet.
Say them out loud. Speaking slows you down and makes you notice the words. A whisper counts.
Set one reminder at your anchor time, for the first few weeks while the habit forms.
Track a streak. A mark on a calendar or a streak counter in an app makes a missed day visible, so you can start again the next morning instead of drifting off.
Refresh them every few weeks. When a line stops meaning anything, swap it for a new one.

sections.h2: How to write affirmations you will keep saying
list: Present tense: "I am learning to rest" rather than "I will rest more".
Believable: a small step you can accept today works better than a big claim that makes you argue back.
Specific: name the thing you care about, such as work, your body, a relationship or money.
Short: one breath long, so you can say it without reading.

sections.h2: Where to put them so you see them
list: Your Lock Screen, where you look dozens of times a day. Our guide shows how to put affirmations on your iPhone Lock Screen.
A sticky note on the mirror or the coffee machine at your anchor spot.
A recording in your own voice, to play on a walk or a commute.
The free affirmation of the day page, which shows a new one every day.
Too many at once. Twenty affirmations turn into a chore; three to five said with attention stick.
No fixed time. "Sometime today" usually means never. Tie it to your anchor.
Quitting after a missed day. A streak is a tool, not a test. Restart the next morning.
Lines you do not believe. If one makes you wince, soften it until it feels possible.
sections.note: Affirmations are a self care habit, not a treatment. If low mood or anxiety gets in the way of daily life, talk to a doctor or a mental health professional.

sections.h2: Make it easier with an app
sections.intro: SayBright is a daily affirmations app for iPhone from Graysmith Labs built around this habit: five free affirmations a day from the topics you choose, a reminder at the time you pick, and streak milestones from 7 to 365 days. You can write your own affirmations for free.
sections.note: Premium adds every category with no daily limit, widgets that change all day, recordings in your own voice and a streak save for one missed day a week.

faq: How do I start a daily affirmation habit?
Tie it to something you already do every day, say three to five short, believable affirmations out loud at that moment, and use a reminder and a streak so a missed day is easy to restart.
How many affirmations should I say a day?
Three to five is plenty to start. Saying a few with attention works better than reading a long list.
What is the best time to say affirmations?
Whenever you will actually do it every day. Mornings work well for many people because the day has not filled up yet.
Should I say affirmations out loud?
Out loud is better if you can. It slows you down and makes you notice the words. A whisper or saying them in your head still counts.
How long does it take to form an affirmation habit?
It varies a lot from person to person. Expect a few weeks of reminders before it feels automatic, and do not worry about the odd missed day.
Can I record affirmations in my own voice?
Yes. Your phone's voice memo app works, and SayBright Premium lets you record any affirmation in your own voice and play it back in the app.
